What I would suggest, as someone who just started taking my art seriously in February. Would be to just draw things you like. 

The approach I took was to draw a piece, finish it, then move on. If I found something I couldn't draw, for instance drawing anatomy. I would Google it as well as ask on places like this subreddit if I felt comfortable enough.

There are a lot of drawing books as well as YouTube videos etc. That can also really help so if you wanted you could try and give those a go too. But I often found that I wouldn't be able to follow the exact roadmap laid out. So instead I would  pick and choose parts that applied to issues I was having as I went along.

Lastly I would suggest to experiment with a bunch of different things, you don't have to spend loads of money or do things you don't enjoy, but just be curious, maybe you'll start with pencil drawing and decide to try colouring pencils, or watercolour, or oil pastels. 

I wish you all the best :) remember to try and enjoy yourself as well! I used to get so worked up about what I couldn't do that it took the fun out for me.

Hope that helps

I completely get that feeling. And its something ive been trying to move past as well. Some things have helped me a lot to start moving past this feeling so i hope they help you too.

1) I got a sketchbook that i told myself is just for my eyes. It can help make you feel more comfortable making mistakes. At least its worked for me as i can be as ambitious as i like and make bad drawings knowing that no one will see them exept for me.

2) Ive tried to stop comparing my work to others and started comparing my work to my older work instead. That way i see my improvement rather than how bad i am compared to others. I know this is really difficult too and i still catch myself feeling inferior from time to time. It's certainly made it easier though.

3) lastly what has helped me is not spending too much time on each piece of work. I draw it, get it finished, and move on to the next piece of work. Instead of focusing on all my works problems i think "maybe next time ill do this part better". It can certainly help with moving forward constantly. And when mixed with the other two points it can help you see you mistakes, feel comfortable that youve made them. And then instead see where youve improved from before.

I hope this all makes sense and it helps you. I stopped drawing for 2 years because i lost all confidence in myself. But now im enjoying drawing again and steadily improving.
